claims.claim: Every connected cograph other than a singleton or a graph with exactly one universal vertex is equivalent to the zero game.
claims.evidence: For every nontrivial connected cograph C, the connected components of its complement are the root-join blocks. A vertex is universal exactly when its complement block is a singleton. If C has at least two universal vertices, pairing two of them covers every vertex. If C has no universal vertex, every complement block has size at least two; choose distinct a,b in one block and c,d in another. Every vertex in the first block belongs to N[c]∩N[d], and every other vertex belongs to N[a]∩N[b]. These disjoint pairs form a pairing dominating set. Remark 9 therefore gives contextual equivalence C=0, not merely standalone scores (0,0). The two cases exhaust the claimed scope. Exact minimax independently confirmed both scores zero and checked the stated pairings on all 1,199 relevant connected labeled cographs through six vertices.
claims.witness: Pairing certificate: two universal vertices when available; otherwise pairs (a,b) and (c,d) chosen from two distinct complement components.
claims.search_method: Structural complement-component proof, followed by exhaustive labeled-cograph enumeration and exact integer minimax through order six.

claims.claim: SHVG on cographs is polynomially equivalent to an explicit open-or-delete scoring game on rooted forests.
claims.evidence: Let C have unique universal vertex u. A name-swapping strategy proves that u weakly dominates every other move in C for either player: compare a strategy starting at x with one starting at u and transpose u,x thereafter. If simulated u receives the same player's color as x, the final coloring is unchanged; otherwise, ownership of u changes in the favorable direction—Maker owning u cannot reduce a nonnegative component score, while Breaker owning u forces that component's score to zero. If Breaker takes u, every closed neighborhood contains a Breaker vertex, so the residual position has both scores zero and is equivalent to deletion. If Maker takes u, put H=C-u. Here |H|≥2, and H has twins a,b. Applying the source twin theorem to both the position on C with u Maker-owned and the empty position on H allows a to be assigned to Maker and b to Breaker. Then b spoils u, while each vertex of H is happy in C exactly when it is happy in H; hence the residual games are contextually equivalent. Recursion gives precisely the stated forest rules and preserves either starting player. Conversely, realize a prize leaf by K1 and an internal node by taking the disjoint union of its child graphs and a zero K2 ballast, then adjoining a universal vertex. With at least one child this new vertex is uniquely universal; a childless zero node can simply be omitted. The construction remains a cograph and has 3 vertices per internal node plus one per prize leaf, so both reductions are polynomial, indeed linear in their structural representations. Exact minimax matched the forward reduction on all 6,039 labeled cographs through six vertices and 320 seeded cographs of orders 7–10, and matched 30 small inverse constructions.
claims.witness: Forward certificate maps K1 to a prize leaf, discards pairing-zero components, and maps each unique-universal component to an open/delete root over the reductions of C-u; the inverse certificate uses a K2 ballast at each internal node.
claims.search_method: Independent strategy-transposition proof, twin-reduction proof, inverse construction, exhaustive exact minimax on small cographs, and seeded larger finite tests.

claims.claim: The cograph game is linear-time solvable when every tree in the reduced forest has outdegree at most two.
claims.evidence: Let A be the prize-leaf game and Z the zero game. After replacing already-classified children by equivalent A/Z games, zero children can be omitted. A node with zero A-children has both scores zero. With one A-child, Maker opening leaves Breaker to move on A and scores zero, while Breaker deletes for zero; Theorem 6 therefore makes the node Z. With two A-children, A+A has score one for either starter and hence is the constant-one game; the parent consequently has Maker option one and Breaker option zero, exactly the game A. This proves the A/Z classification inductively for every binary rooted tree. A top-level forest with z surviving A-types is z isolated prize leaves, giving scores ceil(z/2) and floor(z/2). Cotree/reduced-forest construction and one bottom-up label per node take linear time in the graph representation. Exact minimax agreed with this classification on 2,554 binary forests of total structural size at most eight.
claims.witness: Bottom-up certificate labeling each internal node A exactly when both of its nonzero child labels are A, and Z otherwise; the output is the number z of top-level A labels.
claims.search_method: Induction using contextual zero equivalence and the identity A+A=1, plus exhaustive exact minimax over bounded binary forests.

claims.claim: Reduced forests of height one—equivalently, disjoint unions of stars and isolated vertices after zero components are removed—admit an O(n^2) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: For a multiset S of unopened star sizes and l exposed leaves, unrestricted minimax gives M(S,l)=max(1+B(S,l-1) when l>0, max_{q∈S} B(S-{q},l+q)) and B(S,l)=min(M(S,l-1) when l>0, min_{q∈S} M(S-{q},l)). Adding exposed prize leaves cannot lower Maker's value for either starter, by the source's disjoint-sum bounds. A simultaneous induction on remaining vertices then proves, for j≤k and X∈{M,B}, both X(S+{j},l)≤X(S+{k},l) and X(S+{j},l+k)≥X(S+{k},l+j); checking exposed-leaf moves, moves in S, and the distinguished j/k stars closes the induction. The first inequality makes deleting a largest star optimal for Breaker, and the second makes opening a largest star optimal for Maker. Sorting k1≤...≤kr therefore yields exactly the two displayed draft recurrences. With K equal to the total number of prize leaves, there are O(rK)=O(n^2) reachable table entries, and every transition is constant time. Independent unrestricted minimax matched the largest-star recurrence on 352,716 exhaustive states with at most six stars, sizes at most 12, and exposed-leaf counts at most 12, plus 1,000 larger seeded states with up to eight stars and counts at most 30.
claims.witness: Exchange certificate for every pair j≤k: replacing j by k is Maker-monotone, while retaining j and exposing k is at least as favorable to Maker as retaining k and exposing j.
claims.search_method: Derived the unrestricted minimax recurrence, proved the two exchange inequalities by simultaneous induction, and compared unrestricted versus largest-star minimax over exact finite state spaces.

claims.claim: The pair of standalone scores (Ms,Bs) is insufficient as a cotree dynamic-programming state.
claims.evidence: Exact minimax gives P3 and K1,3 the same standalone pair (1,0). However, their behavior under the same disjoint-union context differs: P3+P3 has pair (1,1), whereas P3+K1,3 has pair (2,1). A compositional cotree state containing only (Ms,Bs) would identify P3 and K1,3 and therefore be forced to give the same result after adjoining P3, contradicting these exact values.
claims.witness: P3 and K1,3, with common context P3: scores are P3=(1,0), K1,3=(1,0), P3+P3=(1,1), and P3+K1,3=(2,1).
claims.search_method: Exact integer/bitmask enumeration of every alternating play on the four explicit graphs.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a classification of SHVG on all cographs by either a polynomial-time algorithm or a matching hardness theorem. The draft proves an exact polynomial equivalence with an open-or-delete rooted-forest game and gives polynomial algorithms for binary and height-one reduced forests, but expressly leaves the unrestricted rooted-forest game unresolved. Thus it does not resolve the entire requested target, while the verified reduction, structural elimination, tractable subclasses, and state obstruction are material and correctly matched partial progress. The final writeup does not assert a full classification, and claimed_resolution="PARTIAL" is therefore ACCURATE rather than overstated or understated.
